items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice lines and the Friday designation
items.text: Puka Nacua (LAR) practiced Wednesday as a limited participant, his first session in about two weeks with the groin, and Sean McVay said he expects him to play at PHI. Davante Adams drew 13 targets at DEN without him. Nacua is not on the Menu; the Friday run ranks him if he practices Thursday. Monitor; Thursday's and Friday's practice lines and the Friday designation.

Keon Coleman (BUF) did not practice Wednesday with the ankle that had him questionable last week, when he played 48 percent of the snaps vs LAC and caught 1 of 2 for 37. DJ Moore drew a team-high 10 targets in that game. Joshua Palmer gets the snaps if Coleman sits. Sit Coleman vs NE either way.

items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice lines and the Friday designation
items.text: Bucky Irving (TB) was limited Wednesday with a glute injury he picked up on the last two drives vs MIN, after the team had said he would not be on the report. The Menu row said he was not on the report; it now carries the flag. He stays RB16 with a rookie quarterback handing off vs GB. Monitor; Thursday's and Friday's practice lines, and have a backup ready.

Ashton Jeanty (LV) is on Wednesday's report with the ankle he had taped at NO and practiced in full. He has 20 or more touches in every game and 16 targets, and Mike Washington Jr. has 15 carries for 102 behind him. Start Jeanty as an RB1 vs KC.

Aaron Jones Sr. (MIN) was listed limited Wednesday as a rest day, not injury related, so the knee from Week 2 is off the report. He has 78 percent of the carries and a 24 percent target share since Jordan Mason went on IR, and MIA has allowed the most points to running backs. Start him as your RB2 vs MIA.

Drake Maye (NE) was added to the injury report Wednesday with the right shoulder and practiced in full; he says it has not affected his arm or his decisions. The line is the problem: 1 touchdown pass, 6 interceptions and 9 sacks in three games, under 13 fantasy points in each. Sit him at BUF.

Chris Godwin (TB) did not practice Wednesday with an ankle injury, and he had already slipped to 62 percent of the snaps vs MIN, third among the receivers behind Ted Hurst III, with 3 catches for 25. He has 10 catches for 111 yards on the season. Sit him vs GB whether or not he plays.

Rico Dowdle (PIT) was ruled out Wednesday for Thursday night at CLE with the toe; he did not practice all week and his right foot was in a walking boot. Jaylen Warren played 90 percent of the snaps and had 20 touches the last time Dowdle sat, and Pittsburgh ran two tight ends on most snaps vs CIN, so the checkdowns run through him. Start Warren as an RB1.

Ben Johnson said Wednesday the Bears have picked their starter vs NYJ and will not say whether it is Tyson Bagent (CHI) or Case Keenum; Bagent is cleared from the concussion and Caleb Williams (hamstring) sat out the walkthrough. Keenum threw for the win at PHI on Monday night. Neither is a fantasy start. Monitor; the Friday practice report and the Sunday inactives for who takes first-team reps.
items.watch: Friday practice report and Sunday inactives

items.text: Lamar Jackson (BAL) was limited Wednesday with a back injury, the first time he has been on the report this season; Jesse Minter called it something small and said he is expected to play vs TEN. Both centers are still out, so a rookie guard snaps to him. He stays QB2 on the Menu with the flag. Monitor; the Thursday practice line and the Friday designation.
items.watch: Thursday practice line and the Friday designation

items.text: Josh Allen (BUF) was not on Wednesday's injury report after the helmet to the left knee vs LAC, and Joe Brady said twice this week he is not concerned. Allen played all 66 snaps in that game. Start him as your QB1 vs NE.

Zay Flowers (BAL) was listed with the hamstring and limited Wednesday, not a full practice, after 21 snaps and 15 routes in Brazil on a pitch count. On 26 routes this season he has 234 yards and a target on 48 percent of them. The snap cap is the risk, not the matchup. Start him as a WR2 vs TEN and check Friday's line.

Mike Evans (SF) sat out Wednesday with the ribs, and Kyle Shanahan said he, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw should all be good to go by Thursday. Evans left the ARI game in the second quarter after the hit. Monitor; Thursday's practice line, and start him as a WR2 vs DEN if it says limited or full.

At JAX the early downs were an even split, and Rhamondre Stevenson, not TreVeyon Henderson (NE), took most of the passing-situation and short-yardage snaps: 33 snaps to 23 and 3 catches to 1. The passing-down case for Henderson does not hold this week. Sit him at BUF; Stevenson stays a RB2.

Mack Hollins drew 9 targets (6 for 87) at JAX to Romeo Doubs' 4 (3 for 49) and led the New England receivers in snaps, so Hollins is the A.J. Brown pivot on the Menu and Doubs (NE) comes down from a WR3. Doubs has 6 catches for 145 in the two games without Brown, 3 catches in each. Flex Doubs; do not start him as a WR3.

Mack Hollins (NE) played 76 percent of the snaps at JAX, the most of any Patriots receiver, and drew 9 targets on 38 dropbacks, 6 catches for 87 yards. A.J. Brown is on IR until about Week 7, so the targets stay open. Add him, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, and flex him at BUF.

Justin Jefferson did not practice Wednesday, and Kyler Murray (MIN) went 15 of 29 for 168 yards with 3 sacks at TB in an offense that scored one touchdown; the defense and special teams won the game. He comes off the Menu's stream line. Sit him vs MIA unless Jefferson practices by Friday.

items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice and the Friday designation
items.text: Justin Jefferson (MIN) is day to day with the ankle sprain and did not practice Wednesday. When he left at TB the targets went to Jordan Addison first, 9 targets for 5 catches, 90 yards and a touchdown; Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton got 2 each. Start Addison as a WR3 either way. Monitor Jefferson; Thursday and Friday practice and the Friday designation.

Jaylen Wright (MIA) was limited at Wednesday's practice with the foot after sitting out Week 3, and he had been working ahead of Ollie Gordon II before he was hurt. Jeff Hafley says every back will have a role. Wright has 3 carries this season. Stash him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB; Thursday and Friday decide whether he is back in the split at MIN.

items.price: a WR2 or a RB2 who catches passes
items.text: Omarion Hampton's (LAC) snap share has gone 58, 63 and 42 percent by week; the Heat Check and Butcher Shop cards listed Week 1 at 80.6 percent and are fixed. The fall is from Week 2, and the routes went 10, 10 and 6 with 3 targets all season while Keaton Mitchell ran 33 routes. The call stands: trade him away and ask for a WR2 or a RB2 who catches passes.

Tre' Harris (LAC) had his best game, 6 of 7 for 76 vs BUF, on his smallest snap share of the season: 58 percent after 75 and 82, because Ladd McConkey came back to 88 percent of the snaps and Quentin Johnston played 87. The targets grew while the role shrank, so he moves from the Market Run adds to the stashes. Stash him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB; he needs a starter to miss time.

Mason Taylor (NYJ) did not practice Wednesday, remains week to week with the thumb and is expected to miss a second straight game at CHI; Adonai Mitchell (finger) is week to week too. Kenyon Sadiq played 57.6 percent of the snaps at DET, ran a route on 58 percent of the dropbacks and drew 8 of 37 targets, so the Menu moves him from a stream to a start at TE16. Start Sadiq as your TE1 at CHI.

Breece Hall (NYJ) sat out Wednesday's practice with the quadriceps and is week to week. Braelon Allen played every snap after Hall left at DET, 4 carries for 14 and 3 catches for 3 yards, and Isaiah Davis has no offensive snap this season; Hall's catches went to Garrett Wilson and Sadiq, not to Allen. Flex Allen at CHI, and if Hall is ruled out Friday, start him as a low RB2.

Geno Smith (NYJ) went 31 of 37 for 321 yards and 3 touchdowns at DET with 5 sacks, and he has completed 75.5 percent with no interception through three games. The Menu had him at QB23 as a sit with no note while the Market Run called him a stream; the two pages now agree. Stream him at CHI if your starter is Mayfield or Dart.

Jalen Hurts (PHI) was checked for a concussion after a late hit at CHI, cleared, and back in after four snaps; he finished 16 of 25 for 153 with 1 interception, 4 rushes for 25 and a sneak score. He has 16 rushes for 87 yards and one rushing touchdown in three games, so the Menu note no longer calls that a floor. He stays QB7. Start him as your QB1 vs LAR.

DK Metcalf (PIT) had 5 targets vs CIN even with Roman Wilson benched for the second half, and he has 98 yards on 24 targets in three games while Pittsburgh leaned on two tight ends (Darnell Washington 47 of 62 snaps). The targets did not consolidate, so both Menu lists now say the same thing. Flex him at CLE Thursday; he is not a WR3 start.

Sam Darnold (SEA) went 31 of 45 for 379 yards and 4 touchdowns with 2 interceptions at WAS in his first game back from the glute injury, and Seattle gained 437 yards at 6.8 a play. The Menu note carried only the picks and sat him while the same page sent Mayfield managers his way. Stream him vs LAC.

Jadarian Price (SEA) had 6 touches on 19 snaps and 11 routes at WAS, third of the three backs in carries and routes, and his fumble came on his third carry with no carry again until the third quarter; he has 2 lost fumbles on 32 touches. Mike Macdonald said Monday the team keeps giving him the ball, but the usage does not support a flex yet. Sit him vs LAC until the first-quarter carries come back.

Emeka Egbuka (TB) has 13 catches for 141 on 20 targets in three games, and his snap share fell from 86 to 74 percent vs MIN while Baker Mayfield was sacked 6 times behind this line; undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starts vs GB. The Menu's receiver list said start and the flex list said sit; both now say flex. Flex him vs GB, and sit him in 10-team leagues.

Tyjae Spears (TEN) did not practice Wednesday with the ankle he aggravated at NYG, though Robert Saleh said there is no concern about him playing at BAL. Starting right guard Fernando Carmona Jr. and backup Jackson Slater went to IR Tuesday, and Michael Carter was signed to the roster. Tony Pollard had 53 percent of the snaps, 80 percent of the early downs and no third-down snap; if Spears sits, the passing downs are his. Flex Pollard at BAL; his Menu row now carries a watch on Spears' Thursday and Friday practice.

items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice, then the Friday designation
items.text: Tyjae Spears (TEN) did not practice Wednesday (ankle) after 26 snaps, 16 routes and 3 carries at NYG, and the coach says he expects him to play at BAL. He runs more routes than Pollard and owns the third downs when active. Monitor Spears; Thursday and Friday practice, then the Friday designation.

Wan'Dale Robinson (TEN) drew a game-high 11 targets at NYG, 7 for 57 and a touchdown, on 29 routes, 81 percent of the dropbacks. The Heat Check and the Menu said his snaps went from 28 to 38; a second snap source has 36, so both pages now cite the route share instead. Claim him, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB; a PPR flex at BAL if the routes hold.

Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Jayden Reed (GB) will have neck surgery and miss the rest of 2026, and Reed went on injured reserve the same day. An IR slot buys nothing in a redraft league now, and nobody inherits his job: the third receiver vs ATL was a three-man rotation, Skyy Moore 27 routes, J. Michael Sturdivant 19 and Bo Melton 19 on 55 dropbacks. Drop Reed in every redraft format.

Nico Collins (HOU) practiced Wednesday as a limited participant, his first session since the hamstring strain that cost him Weeks 2 and 3, and DeMeco Ryans is hopeful he plays vs DAL. He stays WR15 on the Menu with the Q flag, and Dallas has allowed 7 passing touchdowns in three games. Monitor Collins; Thursday's practice and Friday's designation decide it.

The Menu had David Montgomery (HOU) as an RB2 start off one game, 34 snaps to Woody Marks' 20 vs IND. Over three games the snaps are close to even: about level in Week 1, 42 to 38 in Week 2, then 34 to 20. Montgomery is at 2.8 yards a carry and has been hit at or behind the line on 68 percent of his runs, the highest rate in the league. Marks has more targets, 8 to 7. Both Menu lists now read the same. Flex Montgomery vs DAL; he is not an RB2 this week.

Woody Marks (HOU) has 8 targets and 50 routes in three games, and 37 percent of the snaps was Week 3 only; the split was about even in Week 1 and 42 to 38 in Week 2. His role grows when Houston trails, 6 targets in the 20-6 loss to CIN, and he took the goal-line score at IND. Flex him vs DAL in PPR.

The Menu had Daniel Jones (IND) as a sit in London with Josh Downs and Tyler Warren as the whole tree. Keenan Allen had 9 targets too: Downs 11, Warren 10 and Allen 9 took 30 of the 36 attempts vs HOU. Washington has allowed 280.3 passing yards a game, 31st in the league, and a league-high 11 passing touchdowns in three games. Stream Jones vs WAS in London.

Brian Thomas Jr. (JAX) ran 13 to 15 routes vs NE, under half of the dropbacks, on 23 of 62 snaps; he was on the field for 77 percent of the three-receiver snaps and off it in two-tight-end sets. Rookie Josh Cameron matched his 23 snaps and scored. The Menu had Thomas as a flex while the Market Run and Heat Check said drop; the Menu row now reads sit. Sit him @CIN, and in 12-team leagues cut him for any add on the Market Run list.

Jake Ferguson (DAL) is TE15 on the Menu and the row now reads sit instead of stream. His snap share went 76, 60 and 69 percent by week while Brevyn Spann-Ford went 22, 38 and 38, he is fifth on his own team with 11 targets, and he lost a fumble on the opening drive vs BAL. The 3 touchdowns are the whole line, and the Butcher Shop already has him as a sell. Sit him @HOU for any tight end with a steadier target share.

Javonte Williams (DAL) had 19 carries for 98 and a touchdown on 56 snaps, 76 percent, vs BAL, and the Menu row said every touch was his with Malik Davis hurt. Tyler Goodson made his Dallas debut as the No. 2 with 11 snaps and 6 carries for 22, and Emari Demercado did not play a snap. The role is the same; the name behind him changed. Start Williams as your RB2 @HOU.

The Menu's Bo Nix (DEN) note leaned on a rushing floor that has not shown up: 12 carries for 15 yards in three games, with one 1-yard touchdown vs LAR. San Francisco is without Nick Bosa and several defensive linemen, and Arizona ran 87 plays and scored 30 on that front in Week 3, so it is not the tough spot the note called it. Nix is 56 of 93 for 605 yards, 4 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Stream him @SF.

The Menu's Matthew Golden (GB) row said Jayden Reed's absence gives him the routes. He already had them: an 83 percent route share, 25 percent of the targets and 40 percent of the air yards through three games, two of them with Reed active, for 15 catches, 253 yards and a touchdown. Vs ATL he ran 44 routes on 55 dropbacks and drew 12 targets. Start him as your WR2 @TB.

Keenan Allen (IND) faces possible league discipline after a September charge from an August arrest; league policy carries a three-game minimum, none has been announced, the next court date is Oct 26 and he is eligible now. He has 20 targets on 75 routes, 26.7 percent, and took 9 of 36 attempts vs HOU. Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB, and know a ban could land in season.

The Market Run said most of Xavier Worthy's (KC) snaps come without a route. Kansas City had 24 dropbacks on 49 plays @MIA, and his 19 routes are a 79 percent route share, level with Travis Kelce and one more than Rashee Rice. The routes are there; 63 yards on 15 targets in three games with no game above 25 is the problem. Drop him for Sadiq, Harris or Keenan Allen.

Khalil Shakir (BUF) drew 3 targets and caught 1 for 6 yards on 73 percent of the snaps vs LAC while DJ Moore drew a team-high 10. The Menu row said the volume was coming his way; it did not. Sit him vs NE; he comes down the receiver list on Friday's Prep Notes.

DJ Moore (BUF) led Buffalo with 10 targets and caught 6 for 67 on 64 percent of the snaps through the shoulder vs LAC. His Menu rows now carry the targets and agree with each other: start him as a WR3 vs NE, and he is a flex, not a sit, on the flex list.

James Cook (BUF) ran 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown on 67 percent of the snaps and 81 percent of the early downs vs LAC, with 1 target and no catch, while Ty Johnson came back and took the passing downs (15 snaps, 4 of 4 for 50). The Menu note that pinned more handoffs on Allen's knee is gone; the carries are the reason. Start Cook as your RB1 vs NE and expect the catches to stay with Johnson.

Derrick Henry (BAL) ran 26 times for 89 yards (3.4) and 2 touchdowns vs DAL on 67 percent of the snaps, with his 11 inside runs going for 23 yards and two stops on fourth-and-1, and now both centers are out. He has 6 touchdowns in three games and the goal line is still his. Start him as your RB1 vs TEN; the line is why the yardage floor is lower than the rank.

Left guard Damien Lewis (CAR) has a UCL tear in his elbow and is out vs DET, so Corey Bullock makes his first start and Carolina has three backup linemen in front of Bryce Young, the most-pressured quarterback in the league at 47 percent of dropbacks. Young had his foot stepped on at CLE, did not miss a snap, and Dave Canales expects him to play. He stays QB12 on the Menu with 939 passing yards behind him; monitor Thursday and Friday practice for his foot and for Jalen Coker before you commit.
items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice for Young's foot and for Coker

items.text: Mark Andrews (BAL) was not among the players missing Wednesday's practice after the hand injury in Brazil, and his 33 of 64 snaps were an even split with Durham Smythe, which reads like the role, not the hand. He had 5 targets and 3 for 24. Stream him vs TEN if you need a tight end; he is TE14 on the Menu, not a weekly start.

Jeremiyah Love (ARI) out-snapped Tyler Allgeier for the first time in Week 3, 56 snaps (64 percent) to 31, after Allgeier led 60 to 43 percent in Weeks 1 and 2: 21 of the backs' 23 carries for 90, 5 of 5 targets for 19 and a receiving touchdown, 22 routes. Allgeier kept 3 of the 5 goal-line snaps, and the game was a 54-dropback trailing script. Start Love as your RB2 @NYG and watch the first-half split and the goal line.

Harold Fannin Jr. (CLE) drew 9 targets, a 30 percent share, with 45 percent of the air yards, 7 catches for 51 and 2 touchdowns vs CAR on 87 percent of the snaps and 77 percent of the routes; his targets have gone 3, 6, 9 by week. Jerry Jeudy ran 23 routes with no target. Start Fannin as your TE1 vs PIT on Thursday.

Darren Waller (CAR) led Carolina with 8 targets on 28 routes and 39 of 77 snaps at CLE, 5 catches for 51, and his snaps have gone 24, 29, 39 by week with Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out. He is outside the Menu's top 20 tight ends, so this is a streamer's call. Monitor Coker's Friday designation; stream Waller vs DET if Coker is out, and sit him if Coker plays.
items.watch: Jalen Coker's Friday designation; stream Waller vs DET if Coker is out

items.text: Kalif Raymond (CHI) has 23 percent of the targets on 66 percent of the routes and 214 receiving yards through three games, with 9 or more PPR points in each, on more than 60 percent of the snaps every week. The usage is real; the quarterback may change to Tyson Bagent, and the share was built with Case Keenum. Add him in PPR, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, as a WR4 with a floor, not a starter until you see him with Bagent.

Mike Washington Jr. (LV) has 15 carries for 102 yards, 6.8 a carry, with 5 for 54 and a 36-yard touchdown @NO, and the coach has said twice that he earned more opportunities. He has no receiving role. Jeanty still has 81 percent of the backs' carries, so this is a handcuff with a rising early-down share, and the yards per carry back it. Stash him, 3 to 8 percent of FAAB, if you own Jeanty or have a deep bench.

John Harbaugh said Jameis Winston starts vs ARI and that J.J. McCarthy, acquired from MIN for a 2027 fifth-round pick, is the No. 2 while he learns the offense, since Jake Haener was waived the day of the trade. Malik Nabers (NYG) drew 27 percent of the targets in Winston's first start, a nor'easter with 22 team attempts, but caught 5 of 6 for 26 yards at an average depth of target of 1.0. Hold Nabers as a WR2 on volume; what changes the call is McCarthy taking the job, and Week 6 vs NO is the first realistic date for that.
items.why: 27 percent of the targets holds even with a 1.0 average depth of target; the call changes only if McCarthy takes the job, Week 6 vs NO at the earliest.

items.text: Rachaad White (WAS) sat out Wednesday's session in London with the shoulder he hurt vs SEA, and Dan Quinn says he is getting treatment. White played 43 percent of the snaps Sunday, Jacory Croskey-Merritt played 57 percent with 19 carries, and Austin Ekeler made the trip after signing Monday. Croskey-Merritt is the start either way. Monitor White; Thursday's practice report from London.

Jayden Daniels (WAS) was limited in Wednesday's 60-minute jog-through in London, his first practice since he dislocated the left elbow in Week 2, and Dan Quinn says the team will have a definite determination by Friday. Marcus Mariota took every snap vs SEA and threw 3 touchdowns, and he is the WAS quarterback on this week's Menu. Monitor Daniels; Friday's designation.
